subject: NMT
body: Magnetic particle testing detects defects because
options: particles are drawn in by capillary action
a discontinuity causes magnetic flux leakage that attracts particles
explanation: Leakage fields hold particles at the defect.

body: A defect is detected best when it lies at what angle to the magnetic field?
explanation: Inspect in two directions about 90° apart.

subject: NMT
body: A known risk of using prods is
options: arc strikes that can damage the part
explanation: Good contact and correct current reduce the risk.

subject: NMT
body: Which current is better for detecting surface-breaking defects?
explanation: AC concentrates the field near the surface (skin effect).

subject: NMT
body: Which current gives better detection of slightly subsurface defects?
explanation: DC penetrates deeper into the part.

subject: NMT
body: Under ASME Section V, an AC yoke must be able to lift at least
options: 4.5 kg (10 lb) at the maximum pole spacing
explanation: A DC yoke must lift at least 18 kg (40 lb).

subject: NMT
body: Which particles give the highest sensitivity?
explanation: They are viewed under UV-A light.

subject: NMT
body: A pie gauge is used in MT to
options: show the direction of the magnetic field
explanation: A Hall-effect meter measures field strength.

explanation: The residual method relies on leftover magnetism.

subject: NMT
body: Why might a part need demagnetising after MT?
options: Residual magnetism can attract debris or affect later welding and machining
explanation: Arc blow during welding is a common problem.
